Iran's Deputy Parliament Speaker Hamidreza Haji-Babaei said the U.S. must accept the Islamic Republic's 'ten conditions' and that negotiations are no longer about solving a problem but about reaching an agreement with a power.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stated that the U.S. response, received through Pakistan, contains excessive and unreasonable demands, and that details remain under review.
Iran executed three men linked to the January protests.
An official in the UAE told CNN that the Emirates estimate an American and Israeli attack on Iran may occur within the next 24 hours.
An informed European source claimed that the U.S. is preparing to strike Iran soon.
U.S. Central Command announced it redirected 50 commercial vessels enforcing the blockade against Iran.

An Iranian report indicated that President Pezeshkian confronted IRGC Commander Ahmad Vahidi over unauthorized attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, UAE, and Oman, and appealed to Supreme Leader Khamenei to halt the escalation.
President Pezeshkian publicly stated that U.S. demands are impossible, saying America expects Iran to surrender to its unilateral demands.
Iranian President Pezeshkian said 'American demands are impossible and unreachable.'
Iran's Joint Military Command denied carrying out any attack against the UAE in recent days.
Iran's Joint Military Command warned that a 'crushing response' will follow any UAE action against Iran's islands, ports, or coastlines.
Marco Rubio stated that Iran's inflation is 70% and the currency is in total freefall.
The Wall Street Journal reported that China continues to supply Iran and Russia's drone factories with dual-use components despite U.S. sanctions, with thousands of shipments a month.

An Iranian regime historian on state TV called for the assassination of opposition journalists, saying hosts at Manoto TV and Iran International “must understand that their lives are not safe” and “their killing is sanctioned.”
Axios reported that a potential U.S.-Iran agreement could include lifting restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

According to Axios, Washington and Tehran are closer to a deal than at any point since the war began, with key elements including phased rollback of naval restrictions, gradual sanctions relief, release of tens of billions in frozen funds, and a 12- to 15-year enrichment freeze with automatic extensions for violations.
A Pakistani mediation source said the U.S. and Iran are near a one-page deal to end the war.
The Pakistani mediator stated the deal details would include an enrichment freeze, U.S. sanctions relief, and release of frozen funds.
CNBC reported that Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Tehran is evaluating Washington’s 14-point peace proposal.
Iran reportedly ordered its citizens in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and the UAE to return home, saying they may resettle upon return and “repent” for leaving.
Pakistan’s foreign minister said the country is pushing for the U.S.-Iran ceasefire to become a permanent end to the conflict.
Mediators reported a possible Iran deal within 48 hours, while the U.S. military has been ordered to maintain preparations for a prolonged operational posture.
White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett said it seems Iran is making a lot of progress now.
Hassett said yesterday’s mood in the situation room was high, but now progress on Iran talks appears strong.

items.title: 黎巴嫩南部：无人机袭击与以军空袭交织，边境紧张持续
items.description: 黎以边境仍处在高强度对抗中。WIRE 信息显示，真主党无人机袭击造成以军伤亡，以军则称打击了黎巴嫩南部多个真主党目标及隧道设施。北以色列边境社区也面临新的民防限制，说明冲突正在继续影响平民生活。
items.rawSummary: Israeli forces have escalated airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, issuing new evacuation orders for 12 villages and engaging in mutual drone and rocket attacks that wounded two Israeli soldiers on May 6.
items.analysis: Ground operations and airstrikes continue to devastate southern Lebanon; The New York Times, citing satellite imagery, has reported entire towns flattened and over 2,600 killed since March. The IDF said it struck approximately 25 Hezbollah targets over the past day and on May 6 announced it had begun attacking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas after ordering evacuations for 12 villages, most north of the Litani River. Hezbollah has persisted with rocket, mortar, and drone attacks; an explosive drone wounded two Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon, and another drone hit the perimeter fence at Ramim, damaging vehicles without casualties. The IDF intercepted a separate Hezbollah drone and a suspicious aerial target, triggering debris alerts in the Shatula area. Reuters, citing Hezbollah officials, reported several thousand Hezbollah fighters killed since early March, and cross-border sirens and strikes remain frequent.

keyPoints.point: Israeli airstrikes target the towns of Naqoura, Qabrikha, Kfar, and Touline in southern Lebanon.
An Israeli soldier is killed by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
A ceasefire between Hezbollah and Israel goes into effect, though thousands of residents from southern Lebanon begin returning to their homes despite Israeli warnings against doing so.
An Israeli soldier is filmed smashing a statue of Jesus Christ in southern Lebanon; IDF later confirms authenticity and says appropriate measures will be taken.
Israel says two IDF soldiers were punished for smashing the Jesus statue—removed from combat and given 30 days detention—with six others under investigation.
A second French soldier, Corporal Anicet Girardin, dies from wounds sustained in the April 18th Hezbollah attack on a UNIFIL convoy.
Hezbollah attacks a UNIFIL convoy in southern Lebanon with small arms fire, killing one French soldier and wounding another.

Hezbollah resumes attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, conducting three FPV drone operations targeting an artillery position, a command vehicle, and an army position, and claims to have shot down four Israeli reconnaissance drones.
The U.S. State Department urges American citizens to depart Lebanon.
New report indicates widespread looting by Israeli troops in southern Lebanon, taking motorcycles, TVs, and furniture, with commanders reportedly aware but not acting to stop it.

A new round of U.S.-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks is scheduled at the White House, with President Trump reportedly planning to attend, but both sides remain deadlocked over Israeli withdrawal and continued operations against Hezbollah.
Hezbollah fires multiple rockets from Lebanon into Israel, all of which are intercepted by Israeli defenses; no injuries reported.
Hezbollah fires a large volley of rockets into northern Israel, described as a major ceasefire violation.
Hezbollah shoots down an Israeli drone over southern Lebanon using a surface-to-air missile, reportedly downing a second drone as well, despite an announced ceasefire extension.
Hezbollah has significantly ramped up fiber-optic FPV drone attacks in recent weeks, a tactical shift that renders Israeli jamming countermeasures ineffective.
New footage emerges of a Hezbollah fiber-optic FPV drone successfully chasing down and striking an Israeli HMMWV in the town of Qantara.

ISW-CTP assesses that IRGC Commander Ahmad Vahidi has won an internal power struggle in Iran over negotiations, likely reinforcing a maximalist stance that could embolden Hezbollah and increase the risk of conflict with the U.S.
Israel attacks Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon in direct retaliation for ceasefire violations.
Hezbollah launches suicide drones at northern Israel in another ceasefire violation.
Hezbollah sends explosive drones toward Israeli forces in southern Lebanon; no casualties reported according to the Israeli Army.

Assessment indicates Hezbollah is likely conducting smaller-scale, calibrated attacks to threaten Israeli security without triggering major retaliation, while IRGC hardliners continue to dominate Iran's decision-making and block compromise.
The Israeli army destroys solar panels in the town of Debel in southern Lebanon.
The Israeli Air Force launches airstrikes against several Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon in retaliation for Hezbollah suicide drones fired at northern Israel earlier that day.
An Israeli soldier, Sergeant Idan Fooks, 19, is killed by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah targets an Israeli Merkava tank in Beit Lif, southern Lebanon, with an anti-tank guided missile.
Hezbollah targets an Israeli Merkava tank in Beit Lif, southern Lebanon, with an FPV drone.
Footage surfaces of a Hezbollah FPV drone striking an Israeli Merkava Mk.4 main battle tank in southern Lebanon, underscoring continued fiber-optic drone employment.
Hezbollah FPV drone strikes Israeli troops evacuating wounded soldiers, hitting them as they load a helicopter, according to initial reports.
Hezbollah FPV drone narrowly misses an Israeli medevac helicopter evacuating soldiers wounded in an earlier drone attack.
The Israeli army has completely destroyed most of the civilian homes in the town of Beit Lif.
Close footage reveals that the Hezbollah FPV drone strike on Israeli soldiers evacuating wounded troops missed its targets, contradicting earlier claims that the drone hit them.

Hezbollah reportedly plans to increasingly leverage suicide bomber groups in operations against Israeli positions in southern Lebanon, according to Al Jazeera, as reciprocal exchanges continue despite a ceasefire extension.
Hezbollah deploys suicide bomber squads in southern Lebanon, with a senior commander stating the group is returning to 1980s combat tactics to prevent Israeli forces from entrenching.
Hezbollah announces targeting two gatherings of Israeli forces in Naqoura with two FPV drones, achieving confirmed casualties.
Israeli military issues evacuation orders to the residents of 16 villages in southern Lebanon.
Israeli Minister Amichai Chikli states that Israel is establishing a new “border line” with Lebanon, with the IDF continuing to destroy infrastructure during the ceasefire.
Israel's Education Minister visits the family of Sgt. Idan Fooks, who was killed by Hezbollah on April 26, and personally delivers his high school diploma to his parents.
Two Lebanese Army soldiers are wounded as a result of an Israeli targeting in Majdal Zoun, south Lebanon.
IDF troops in Lebanon are improvising solutions to counter Hezbollah drones, indicating the ineffectiveness of existing countermeasures.
A 3-year-old girl, Mila Zayyat, and her mother were reportedly killed by Israeli forces in their home in southern Lebanon.

Iran is expected to submit a new proposal to the United States in the coming days, but is reportedly unwilling to concede on the Strait of Hormuz or its nuclear program, with IRGC hardliners consolidating around demanding an end to the naval blockade first.
Israeli airstrikes hit targets in southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah reportedly shoots down another Israeli UAV in southern Lebanon using a surface-to-air missile.
A Hezbollah drone struck an Israeli military vehicle near Shomera in northern Israel, causing a fire and secondary explosions; approximately 12 IDF soldiers were wounded.
The Israeli military stated it struck buildings in southern Lebanon where Hezbollah operatives were active, claiming the sites were used to plan attacks against Israeli forces and territory.
The Israeli military announced that Sgt. Liam Ben Hamo was killed by an explosive drone in southern Lebanon, and one other soldier was moderately wounded.
The Israeli military warned residents in 15 towns in southern Lebanon to evacuate and remain at least one kilometer away ahead of planned airstrikes targeting Hezbollah-linked infrastructure.
Israeli airstrikes struck Klaouieh, Arzoun, and Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon.
The Israeli military said it destroyed a 140-meter Hezbollah tunnel in Ras Bayda, southern Lebanon, using 24 tons of explosives.
Israel's Home Front Command reclassifies northern border communities as yellow zones starting next week, imposing new restrictions on gatherings and educational activities.
Hezbollah drones triggered sirens in Rosh Hanikra, northern Israel; the Israeli Air Force intercepted at least four Hezbollah drones, and a fifth interception is under review.
The Israeli military stated that over 40 Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon, including command centers, were struck and destroyed in the past day.
Attendance at the Lag B’Omer pilgrimage on Mount Meron is capped at 200 people as part of tightened restrictions in northern Israel.
The Israeli military reported that two IDF soldiers were lightly wounded in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon.

The Israeli military said a drone heading toward IDF forces in southern Lebanon was intercepted, while Hezbollah also fired a rocket and an explosive drone that landed near IDF positions with no casualties.

The Israeli military released footage of a firefight in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, and stated that its 98th Division killed around 200 Hezbollah operatives and destroyed 900 infrastructure sites in the town in recent weeks, including a booby-trapped stadium.
IDF photos of weapons seized from Hezbollah in Bint Jbeil show a U.S. passport and passport photo booklets among the confiscated arms.
More than ten interceptor missiles were fired from Israel toward Lebanon since the morning, reflecting heightened air defense activity.
The Israeli military reported that IDF forces raided Hezbollah sites in the Rashaf area near Bint Jbeil, seizing hand grenades, rifles, ammunition, and a Kornet missile.
The Israeli military said a rocket fired at its forces in southern Lebanon was intercepted, and an interceptor was launched at a suspected aerial target in the area.
The Lebanese Health Ministry reports at least 13 people killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon.
The Israel Defense Forces says it carried out around 50 strikes in southern Lebanon targeting Hezbollah infrastructure, and reports rocket fire toward its forces with no casualties.
Sirens sounded in Yiftah, northern Israel, over a suspected hostile aircraft were later confirmed a false identification.
The IDF published footage of an airstrike on an armed Hezbollah rocket launcher in southern Lebanon.
The IDF stated that approximately 120 Hezbollah targets were struck in southern Lebanon over the weekend, including 70 military buildings and 50 infrastructure sites.
The IDF reported that 50 Hezbollah buildings were leveled in southern Lebanon on May 1.

The IDF releases footage of recent strikes in southern Lebanon showing drone strikes eliminating armed Hezbollah operatives in two incidents and follow-on airstrikes on buildings where additional operatives were spotted.
Rockets were launched from Lebanon toward Avivim in northern Israel; at least one was intercepted, with further results under review, as cross-border exchanges continue.
Additional Israeli airstrikes were reported across southern Lebanon, with Israeli Air Force jets targeting areas in the region as cross-border operations continued.
The IDF reported uncovering and demolishing an 80-metre Hezbollah tunnel in eastern southern Lebanon that contained multiple living quarters, after combat engineers fully mapped it.

The IDF reported that Hezbollah launched rockets and explosive drones at IDF troops in southern Lebanon, impacting near forces without causing injuries; an interceptor was fired at an additional drone and the interception result is under review.
The IDF says its 401st Brigade forces discovered over 100 Hezbollah weapons caches in southern Lebanon in the past week.
The IDF stated that the Israeli Air Force eliminated Hezbollah operatives who were moving weapons near IDF forces in Lebanon.

The New York Times reported, citing satellite imagery, that entire towns near the border including Bint Jbeil have been flattened and dozens of villages heavily damaged since March, with more than 2,600 people killed and over a million displaced.

Kan 11 reported that a Hezbollah explosive drone crashed intact near an IDF unit in the buffer zone in Lebanon, carrying an optical fiber spool, an RPG warhead, and a battery pack; no injuries were reported.

Hezbollah was reported to be increasingly using FPV drones against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, with Israeli officials acknowledging a lack of effective countermeasures; Prime Minister Netanyahu convened a security meeting to address the threat.

Hezbollah fired several rockets at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon, triggering sirens in the border community of Manara; one rocket was intercepted, others hit open areas, and no injuries were reported. The IDF also launched interceptors at suspected Hezbollah drones, with results under review.
Reuters, citing two Hezbollah officials and a third source, reported that several thousand Hezbollah fighters have been killed since March 2.
Hezbollah released footage claiming to show an FPV drone strike on an Israeli armored personnel carrier in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon.
Sirens sounded in northern Israel and air defenses were activated amid ongoing cross-border attacks from Lebanon.

The IDF stated that 7th Brigade forces eliminated 10 Hezbollah fighters over the past two days across multiple incidents in southern Lebanon, and destroyed a loaded launch site, weapons storage infrastructure, and military buildings; the IAF separately struck Hezbollah infrastructure after an anti-tank missile was fired at Israeli forces, with no casualties.
A popular coastal restaurant known as 'The Boat' was demolished amid Israeli military action in southern Lebanon.

Hezbollah released footage claiming FPV drone strikes on two Israeli Namer APCs, a Merkava Mk.4M tank, and an M113 at IDF staging areas in Lebanon; some Israeli units were reported to have started camouflaging vehicles in a basic and inconsistent manner.

Two Golani Reconnaissance soldiers were moderately wounded in a firefight with Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon; the IDF said the clash began shortly after 11:00 AM, and the IAF struck several Hezbollah military structures and an anti-tank position in the area.

The IDF reported that Givati Brigade reconnaissance troops raided a Hezbollah rocket-launching site in southern Lebanon, capturing dozens of rockets, assault rifles, RPGs and primed launchers that were aimed at troops and at Israel.
The IDF issued evacuation warnings for six villages in southern Lebanon, citing Hezbollah ceasefire violations, and ordered residents to move at least 1,000 meters to open areas immediately.
Airstrikes were reported in southern Lebanon following the evacuation warnings.
Hezbollah operatives launched an anti-tank guided missile at Israeli forces in southern Lebanon; no injuries were caused and the IDF struck the launch site shortly after.
Israeli forces said they struck two Hezbollah operatives attempting to flee on a motorcycle in southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah was reported to have launched FPV drone attacks in southern Lebanon, one targeting a group of three Israeli soldiers and another striking an Israeli HMMWV.
The IDF released footage of an FPV drone approaching and neutralizing an Iranian-made Falaq-1 rocket launcher in southern Lebanon.

The IDF said it eliminated multiple Hezbollah operatives and struck roughly 25 targets in southern Lebanon over the past 24 hours, including weapons depots and military structures, while intercepting additional aerial targets.
The IDF issued evacuation warnings for 12 villages in southern Lebanon, most north of the Litani River, ordering residents to move at least 1 km away ahead of airstrikes on Hezbollah targets.
A Hezbollah rocket attack was reported in northern Israel.
The IDF reported firing an interceptor at a suspicious aerial target over southern Lebanon, with alerts activated in the Shatula area of northern Israel due to possible falling debris.
An explosive drone hit the perimeter fence at Ramim near an IDF post in northern Israel; no casualties reported but vehicles were damaged.

The IDF reported two soldiers wounded in a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in southern Lebanon; one sustained moderate injuries, the other light. A separate Hezbollah drone was intercepted over southern Lebanon.
The IDF announced that strikes on Hezbollah military sites in southern Lebanon were underway.

items.title: 美国侧面：油价与战争成本正在倒逼政策选择
items.description: 美国国内也在承受中东战事外溢压力。WIRE 信息显示，油价高位运行、战争成本估算上升，同时白宫仍在听取新的对伊朗打击和地面行动选项。对华盛顿而言，军事压力、国内成本和外交回旋空间正在同时收紧。
items.rawSummary: The United States is reportedly close to finalizing a preliminary agreement with Iran to end the conflict and begin nuclear talks, as President Trump conditions an end to military operations on Iran's compliance while warning of intensified strikes if talks fail; domestically, a White House-area shooting and deteriorating economic indicators added to the tense environment.
items.analysis: Axios reported that the White House is close to a preliminary agreement with Iran to halt hostilities and launch nuclear talks, with subsequent details indicating a 14-point memorandum of understanding that would include a uranium enrichment moratorium, sanctions relief, release of frozen funds, and a 30-day negotiation period. President Trump stated that if Iran agrees to the deal, Operation Epic Fury will end, but if not, bombing will resume at a higher intensity; he had earlier declared Iran 'has no chance' and should 'waive the white flag.' Secretary of State Rubio warned that Chinese companies ignoring U.S. sanctions on Iran will face secondary measures ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. A shooting near the White House prompted a brief lockdown after Secret Service officers shot an individual who pulled a gun near the Washington Monument, with one person hospitalized. Economic strain continues with the Leading Economic Index falling and its ratio to coincident indicators reaching 0.84, a level last seen during the 2008 financial crisis, while the SEC advanced a plan to end mandatory quarterly earnings reporting.

keyPoints.point: White House press secretary said only the president knows where things stand with Iran and what he will do.
President Trump called Iran's call for civilians to gather near energy stations illegal.
The White House stated President Trump has been made aware of Pakistan's ceasefire proposal and a response will come.
Senator Lindsey Graham called for a congressional review process for any ceasefire or peace agreement with Iran.
The White House announced President Trump will discuss the possibility of the US leaving NATO with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.
Israel excluded France from upcoming direct talks with Lebanon scheduled in Washington, citing French initiatives against Israeli operations and a lack of willingness to help disarm Hezbollah.
Iranian officials stated the US is continuing with irreconcilable demands in talks.
The U.S. State Department revoked the green cards of three Iranian nationals linked to the regime.
Lebanese President expressed hope that upcoming direct talks with Israel in Washington will result in a ceasefire.
A preparatory meeting between Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors, hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is scheduled at the State Department.
The first direct talks in decades between Israel and Lebanon commenced in Washington, hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
U.S. Central Command reported that no ships have made it past the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports since it began in March.
The United States and Iran may hold a second round of negotiations this week amid the ongoing ceasefire.
The first direct talks between Israel and Lebanon in Washington ended after more than three hours, with both sides describing them as positive.
The U.S. Senate scheduled votes on asserting war powers regarding Iran and on blocking arms sales to Israel.
The White House announced it will hold a call with U.S. oil executives on Thursday.
U.S. President Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, brokered following direct talks, beginning Thursday.
President Trump stated he will invite the leaders of Israel and Lebanon to the White House for their first meaningful talks since 1983.
Israeli media reported top officials are increasingly frustrated with the U.S. ceasefire approach, as the deal was announced before UN Security Council approval.
The White House is investigating the strange deaths and disappearances of ten scientists involved in military research for the U.S. government.
A shooting was reported near the Waterfront Metro station in Washington D.C.
A second round of direct talks between Israel and Lebanon is set to take place in Washington.
The U.S. delegation, including Vice President JD Vance, did not depart for scheduled peace talks with Iran in Pakistan.
U.S. oil prices surged above $90 per barrel following confirmation that the U.S. delegation had not departed for Iran talks.
Vice President JD Vance attended White House policy meetings on the stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations.
Israeli media reported it is unlikely the U.S. and Iran will find points of convergence to enable a long-term ceasefire.
An assessment revealed the U.S. military has heavily depleted key missile stockpiles during the recent war, creating a near-term strategic vulnerability.
The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control announced updates to its sanctions list, adding Iranian-linked individuals and entities.
President Trump convened a high-level meeting with Vice President Vance, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, and Joint Chiefs Chair Gen. Dan Caine.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived at the White House alongside Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived at the White House.
U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee was recalled to Washington D.C.
The White House presented Congress with a record $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget request, a 42% increase focused on munitions and hardware.
The White House convened a meeting with Trump, Vance, Rubio, Hegseth, and Caine, settling on seeking a ceasefire extension with Iran.
President Trump publicly attacked the Wall Street Journal and defended his administration's record on Iran.
U.S. officials stated President Trump is offering Iran a limited 3-5 day window to respond with a clear negotiating position, describing it as a final opportunity.
The White House developed a list of NATO countries to potentially punish for refusing to back the Iran war.
U.S. Secretary of the Navy John C. Phelan was fired by the Pentagon, with Undersecretary Hung Cao assuming duties as acting Secretary.
The U.S. Senate blocked an Iran war powers resolution for the fifth consecutive time.
Reports indicated the firing of the Secretary of the Navy was linked to tensions over modernization, shipbuilding delays, and chain-of-command disputes.
President Trump stated he is not anxious to make a deal and all pressure is on Iran.
The U.S. accused China of industrial-scale theft of U.S. AI technology, warning it could raise tensions ahead of a planned summit.
DOJ detains U.S. Soldier accused of $400,000 bet on Maduro's removal.
Large plume of smoke visible near the U.S. Capitol building, bus fire reported.
Pentagon exploring options to punish NATO allies that did not support US operations against Iran.
In Washington, D.C., 20,000 teddy bears were displayed as part of a protest calling on Russia to return Ukrainian children.
DOJ announces arrest of 25 members and associates of the Mexican Mafia prison gang on federal indictments.
The US and EU signed a deal to cooperate on critical minerals.
Bus crash near the Pentagon injures 23, including 10 Department of War personnel.
Administration considers using the Defense Production Act to bail out Spirit Airlines, citing rising jet fuel costs from the Iran war.
Rep. Jim Jordan investigates ActBlue over suspected foreign donations.
New immigration guidance allows officials to deny green cards based on political views, including participation in pro-Palestinian protests.
Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is expected to travel to Washington in mid-May for a potential summit with Lebanese President Michel Aoun.
Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao pledged to defend the homeland, support sailors, and build more ships.
Reports indicate FBI Director Kash Patel is increasingly expected to be removed.
President Trump was rushed off stage by Secret Service during the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were fired.
The suspected shooter was killed in the lobby of the White House Correspondents Dinner event.
Following evacuation, the dinner hosts announced the program would resume; Vice President Vance was confirmed uninjured.
President Trump released a statement following the shooting.
The assailant, armed with a long rifle and multiple magazines, attempted to charge through the magnetometer screening area and fired at Secret Service before being shot dead.
A law enforcement officer was shot in the chest but saved by a bulletproof vest.
Trump announced law enforcement requested the premises be vacated; a press conference was scheduled and the dinner would be rescheduled.
Conflicting reports emerged indicating the suspected shooter was alive and in custody, contradicting earlier information.
The shooter was identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen from Torrance, California.
A protester wearing a keffiyeh reportedly rushed the motorcade in Washington, D.C., and was arrested just before the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting.
Mexican President Sheinbaum expressed relief that President Trump and his wife were safe.
The FBI confirmed the suspect is in custody and was armed with a shotgun and a handgun, contradicting earlier reports of a long rifle.
President Trump released CCTV footage of the attack and stated a Secret Service officer was saved by his bulletproof vest.
President Trump released a photo of the suspected shooter, Cole Tomas Allen.
Reports indicated the shooter was a supporter of former Vice President Kamala Harris.
At a press conference, President Trump stated the shooting would not deter him from winning the war in Iran and described the suspect as a 'whackjob' lone wolf.
President Trump stated he does not think the suspect can be linked to the situation in Iran.
President Trump declared the shooting will not deter the U.S. from winning the war in Iran.
D.C. Police Chief reported the suspect was armed with a hunting rifle, a pistol, and several knives.
The FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force arrived at the shooting scene.
D.C. Mayor stated there is no reason to believe another person is involved in the incident.
D.C. Police Chief confirmed the suspected shooter was not struck by gunfire and is uninjured.
President Trump issued a statement asking all Americans to recommit to resolving their differences peacefully.
The suspect was charged with felony firearms and assault charges against a federal officer.
FBI Director Kash Patel stated the investigation will thoroughly examine the individual's background.
U.S. AAG Todd Blanche announced the suspect will appear in court tomorrow.
Indian Prime Minister Modi expressed relief and unequivocally condemned violence following the shooting.
The FBI arrived at the California home of the shooter to execute a search.
U.S. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated the suspect was determined to inflict the maximum amount of harm.
FBI SWAT personnel entered the California home of the suspected shooter.
The gunman confessed that he was targeting President Trump's officials.
Authorities obtained a warrant and breached the California home linked to the shooter.
The gunman clarified he intended to target Trump administration officials broadly, not specifically mentioning the president.
Polling and Senate vote results reveal a historic shift in U.S. public opinion, with greater popular support for Palestine than Israel.
US markets anticipate significant reaction to the cancellation of US-Iran talks, with oil prices surging.
The shooter's manifesto explicitly named Trump administration officials as targets and contained anti-Trump and anti-Christian content.
Discussions at the White House considered whether President Trump may need to wear a bulletproof vest at future public events.
The shooter was identified as having attended a 'No Kings' protest in California and was linked to a group called 'Wide Awake'.
Food inflation data shows a sharp acceleration, with average inflation for food and beverage companies surging 7.9% year-over-year in March.
President Trump is scheduled to appear on 60 Minutes to provide a detailed account of the previous night's shooting.
The shooter's manifesto outlined a plan to target Trump administration officials prioritized from highest-ranking to lowest, while specifically exempting FBI Director Kash Patel.
In the manifesto, the shooter criticized Secret Service security at the event.
President Trump, speaking on 60 Minutes, revealed that he likely slowed Secret Service evacuation efforts during the shooting.
The White House Correspondents' Dinner was held with a lower level of security than typically used for events attended by top U.S. leaders.
President Trump slammed a CBS reporter as a 'DISGRACE' after she made reference to the term 'pedophile' from the shooter's manifesto.
A new bill (H.R. 8445) was introduced to extend U.S. legal protections to Americans serving in the Israeli army.
President Trump is convening top officials to discuss next steps on Iran amid the negotiation deadlock, including a potential resumption of the bombing campaign.
The sister of WHCD shooter Cole Tomas Allen revealed he was increasingly radical and hid firearms at their parents' Maryland home.
Vice President JD Vance privately raised doubts about the Pentagon's portrayal of U.S. weapons stockpile strength in the Iran war.
Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that President Trump spoke with the wounded Secret Service agent following the shooting.
The White House described the shooting as the third major assassination attempt against Trump in two years.
Investigators are probing the WHCD shooter's possible ties to Stacey Abrams' Fair Fight Action and Black Lives Matter.
President Trump's national security team is discussing Iran's latest proposal, which Iran had delivered to Pakistan three days ago.
Cole Tomas Allen, the WHCD shooter, was officially charged with attempting to assassinate President Trump.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla of the United Kingdom arrived at Joint Base Andrews for a scheduled meeting with President Trump.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla's motorcade arrived at the White House for tea with President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump.
Congressional Democrats moved to force a sixth Iran War Powers vote, scheduling it for Tuesday evening.
The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump and his national security team are skeptical of Iran's latest proposal.
Senate Republicans are increasingly losing confidence in Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Over 1,110 TSA officers have resigned since the DHS shutdown began on February 14.
Cole Tomas Allen faces up to life in prison after being formally charged with the attempted assassination of the president.
President Trump released a statement on Iran as U.S. oil prices rose above $100 per barrel.
Google dropped from Pentagon's drone swarm selection process.
King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress during his state visit.
Reuters reported that U.S. intelligence agencies have been directed to assess the likelihood that Iranian decision-makers will react adversely if President Trump declares a unilateral victory.
The Pentagon asked Congress to formally rename the Department of Defense to the 'Department of War'.
Former FBI Director James Comey was charged with threatening to harm President Trump in an Instagram post.
An arrest warrant was issued for former FBI Director James Comey.
A resolution to prevent President Trump from launching strikes on Cuba was rejected in the U.S. Senate.
President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump hosted King Charles III and Queen Camilla for the White House state dinner.
The Pentagon is considering outsourcing warship design and building to Korea and Japan, according to USNI News.
President Trump met with oil executives as gasoline prices rose to about $4.18 per gallon, according to Axios.
U.S. oil prices surged toward $105 per barrel ahead of earnings reports and a Federal Reserve rate decision.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered opening remarks before the House Armed Services Committee on the requested $1.7 trillion defense budget.
The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged in its final policy decision under Chair Jerome Powell.
The Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady included four dissenting votes, the highest since 1992, and dropped its easing bias.
The Supreme Court is weighing President Trump's authority to end migrant protections.
U.S. 10-year Treasury note yield rose above 4.40% while U.S. oil prices surged above $108 per barrel.

CBS News reported that investigators determined the Secret Service officer shot during the dinner was hit by the suspect's bullet, not friendly fire, and the bullet likely struck a phone inside his vest.
The Pentagon's comptroller told the House Armed Services Committee that the current estimated cost of the Iran War is $25 billion.
Axios reported that President Trump is slated to receive a briefing from CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper on new military options against Iran.
U.S. oil prices surged above $109 per barrel, a 28% increase in eight trading days.
Retired Admiral William McRaven expressed concern that recent Pentagon leadership dismissals may cause senior officers to fear speaking truth to power.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla arrived at the White House for a formal farewell hosted by President Trump and the First Lady.
A deadline nears for President Trump to either end the Iran war or present a case to Congress for its extension.
The U.S. Senate banned senators from trading on prediction markets.
The U.S. House passed a DHS funding bill, sending it to President Trump.
The DHS shutdown, which began in February, is set to end after the House passed a funding bill covering most of the agency, including TSA.
The White House stated that 'Mythos' is not a doomsday device.
The U.S. House voted to end the DHS shutdown by funding the agency except ICE and Border Patrol.
President Trump announced he will remove tariffs and restrictions on whiskey trade involving Scotland and Kentucky.
President Trump called for terminating the Senate filibuster to pass the Save America Act.
President Trump invited the newly elected Iraqi Prime Minister to Washington D.C.
The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia released footage showing Cole Allen shooting a Secret Service officer during the attempted assassination.
Reports indicated President Trump is seriously considering renewed combat operations against Iran.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro released footage showing Cole Allen rushing past security at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.

Air defense activity was reported over Tehran, described as countering surveillance drone threats, on the night President Trump was briefed by CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper on military options against Iran.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro released additional security footage showing Cole Allen walking through the Hilton Hotel the day before the shooting.
Following the briefing, President Trump claimed Iran wants a deal 'badly,' and a 24-hour clock was noted ahead of the deadline to present the administration's case to Congress on the Iran war.
President Trump revived a variant of the Keystone XL pipeline and granted a cross-border permit.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla participated in a wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery, marking the final day of their state visit.
U.S. officials stated CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper and Joint Chiefs Chair Gen. Dan Caine briefed President Trump on Iran military options for 45 minutes.
CCTV footage from the White House Correspondents' Dinner showed a K9 unit handler appearing to have a conversation with suspect Cole Tomas Allen at a checkpoint.
Transatlantic tensions have grown as President Trump has recently attacked European leaders, worsening diplomatic relations with Washington's allies.
The U.S. Department of Justice released footage showing Cole Allen opening fire on a Secret Service officer after breaching security at the Washington Hilton.
The FBI announced 25 convictions in a $215 million Nigerian-linked fraud scheme targeting over 1,000 victims across 47 states.
The U.S. Department of War announced it is partnering with SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and Oracle to deploy AI on classified networks.
President Trump announced the U.S. is raising tariffs on cars and trucks imported from the EU to 25%, citing the EU's non-compliance with a trade deal.
Chinese naval forces conducted major deployments in the South China Sea and West Pacific, likely in response to the ongoing Balikatan 2026 combined exercises.

USFK Commander Xavier Brunson proposed establishing South Korea as a regional sustainment hub to improve U.S. operational efficiency in the Indo-Pacific, which could clarify South Korea's role in a Taiwan contingency.
Taiwan's special defense budget remains stalled due to partisan gridlock, despite increased U.S. pressure to pass it, with divisions within the KMT further complicating efforts.
President Trump notified Congress that hostilities with Iran that began on February 28 have terminated.

The Financial Times reported that Washington warned allies including the UK, Poland, Lithuania, and Estonia to expect delays in U.S. weapons deliveries, as the war with Iran strains American stockpiles.
The U.S. State Department approved over $8.6 billion in military sales to Israel, Qatar, Kuwait, and the UAE, including Patriot systems, APKWS rockets, and a battle command system.
US Representative Randy Fine stated 'We don't want Armenians to be able to serve in Congress.'
Spirit Airlines filed for bankruptcy and ceased all operations after 33 years, canceling all flights.

The U.S. government announced a relief plan for Spirit Airlines customers and employees, with major carriers capping ticket prices, offering reduced fares, and providing preferential employment interviews.
The average U.S. gasoline price surged to $4.43 per gallon, a 61% increase since December, projected to cost Americans an additional $90 billion annually.

The U.S. Treasury General Account balance rose to approximately $1 trillion, the highest since April 2021, driven by spring tax collections, while total federal debt briefly dipped below $39 trillion before T-bill issuance is expected to accelerate again.
President Trump stated that renewed strikes on Iran are an option that could happen.
Washington expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's enriched uranium proposal and is set to respond soon.
Kan News reported that President Trump said he reviewed and rejected Iran's new proposal, and described the military situation as 'going very well.'
CNN reported that US Envoy Witkoff stated the United States is conducting diplomatic talks with Iran.

Nick Stewart, a proponent of aggressive sanctions and potential military force from the FDD think tank, was added to the U.S. Iran nuclear negotiation team, joining Vice President Vance, Jared Kushner, and envoy Steve Witkoff.
The White House was placed on lockdown after reports of shots fired nearby.
An all-clear was given at the White House following the lockdown.

The U.S. Secret Service reported they were involved in a shooting near 15th St and Independence Ave, with one person shot by law enforcement; no details on motive or the person's condition were immediately available.
Fox News reported that the individual shot by Secret Service had pulled a gun near the Washington Monument and was taken to a hospital.

The Conference Board's Leading Economic Index fell 0.6% month-over-month in March, its seventh decline in eight months, and the ratio of leading to coincident indicators dropped to 0.84, matching the 2008 Financial Crisis low.
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and General Dan Caine are scheduled to hold a briefing on Operation Epic Fury at 8 a.m. ET.
The Washington Post reported that over two dozen House Democrats are urging the Trump administration to acknowledge Israel's long-suspected nuclear weapons program.
President Trump asserted that Iran 'has no chance' and said Iranian leaders acknowledge this when they talk to him.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission advanced a plan to end mandatory quarterly earnings reporting requirements for companies.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that Chinese companies ignoring U.S. sanctions on Iran will face secondary sanctions, ahead of a planned Trump-Xi summit.

items.rawSummary: Amid the ongoing naval blockade, an intercepted aid flotilla, and a U.S. plan to shrink its Gaza coordination hub, the IDF struck two armed Hamas operatives in a northern Gaza airstrike, while broader military operations and political tensions continue.
items.analysis: Israel’s navy intercepted a civilian flotilla attempting to break the blockade, insisting all participants were removed unharmed, but activist Hüseyin Oral later alleged he was beaten and robbed while detained, creating conflicting accounts. Reuters reported the US is closing its main Gaza coordination hub and folding it into a smaller international force, while Israel expanded its restricted military zone to roughly two-thirds of Gaza, complicating aid delivery. The war’s financial cost has reached NIS 405 billion amid political turbulence as Netanyahu posted AI-generated videos of rivals and Bennett and Lapid formed a united electoral challenge. Hamas’s security force released video of an alleged ambush on anti-Hamas militiamen, and later footage showed a fighter, Karim Arja, attempting to mine an IDF tank before being spotted and reportedly killed. The IDF has continued targeting operatives: earlier it killed three in southern Gaza and its 205th Brigade recently concluded a northern operation destroying eight tunnels; it also confirmed killing two more Hamas operatives over the weekend. On May 6, the IDF struck two armed Hamas operatives from the air as they moved through building ruins toward Israeli forces in northern Gaza. The Israeli Foreign Ministry said a USAID Inspector General investigation confirmed UNRWA staff, including teachers and a social worker, were involved with Hamas and the Oct. 7 massacre, describing it as systematic embedding of terror within the agency.

keyPoints.point: A senior U.S. official warns that without a breakthrough soon, the war in Gaza could resume within days.
Brazilian President Lula condemns the Israeli operation in Gaza as a genocide and a 'very big lie,' comparing it to the invasions of Iraq and Libya.
Rare testimonies from inside Gaza emerge, detailing allegations of widespread sexual abuse, blackmail for aid, and exploitation by Hamas members against vulnerable displaced civilians.
The band The Strokes closes its Coachella set with a video condemning U.S. foreign policy and Israeli bombings in Gaza, highlighting the conflict's global cultural resonance.
Israel is reported to be preparing for a renewed phase of intense fighting across Gaza at the start of next month, following Hamas's refusal to disarm.
Rachel Goldberg-Polin, mother of hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin, speaks publicly about her grief after being told her son was murdered by Hamas after a year in captivity.
A terrorist who infiltrated Kibbutz Nir Oz on October 7 is killed near the Yellow Line in the southern Gaza Strip after approaching Israeli forces.
Israeli Defense Minister Katz warns of possible escalation with Iran, stating that targets have been marked and Israel is prepared to renew the war against Iran pending U.S. approval.
Senior Israeli officials held a recent meeting with Netanyahu to prepare contacting President Trump to obtain permission to resume hostilities against Iran, according to Channel 13.
Dozens of additional American aerial refueling aircraft arrive in Israel, providing capacity to support long-range strike missions.
Trump announces the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire has been extended for three weeks.
Trump states that Israel must defend itself if attacked but should act carefully and surgically.
More than 250 Bnei Menashe immigrants from India arrive in Israel, settling in northern Israel as part of a larger immigration plan with thousands more expected by 2030.

Former UN Special Rapporteur Michael Lynk accuses Israel of apartheid and genocide in Gaza, stating over 70,000 Palestinians have been killed since October 2023, 83% civilians, and that the violence has surpassed apartheid South Africa.
Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announce plans to form a united political party for the upcoming Israeli elections.
A massive brawl breaks out at a Gaza wedding as tribes debate whether Hamas made a mistake carrying out the October 7 massacre; Hamas, not yet disarmed per the ceasefire, was providing security.

Jusoor News and human rights organizations in Gaza report an epidemic of sexual abuse and child pregnancy under Hamas rule, with video testimonies describing sexual blackmail for aid, abuse by Hamas members, and up to 60,000 vulnerable women.
An Israeli soldier shows footage of Beit Hanoun in northern Gaza, completely destroyed with no houses left standing.

A large civilian flotilla of 60-70 vessels and up to 3,000 participants from over 100 countries, having departed Spain and France and regrouped in Sicily, is crossing the Mediterranean toward Gaza to deliver humanitarian aid and challenge Israel's naval blockade; Israel labels the flotilla Hamas-linked, imposes sanctions, and indicates it will likely intercept.

Ukraine officially requests Israel to take action against the vessel PANORMITIS, suspected of carrying grain illegally transported from occupied Ukraine, based on a Ukrainian court arrest order; Ukraine urges Israel to respond seriously.

Bank of Israel Governor Amir Yaron reports that the war's cost has reached NIS 405 billion (~$137 billion) since October 7, with debt rising from roughly 60% to 70% of GDP and defense spending surging 130% to NIS 143 billion, warning of a 'trauma economy' if trends persist.
The Israeli Navy begins intercepting the Gaza-bound civilian flotilla; crew are ordered to kneel, communications are jammed, an SOS is sent, and drones are overhead.
Israel reports that drugs and condoms were found on the intercepted flotilla.
Netanyahu posted AI-generated videos portraying his electoral opponents as Arabs.
A man named Alex Sinclair was arrested in Israel for wearing a kippah with both Israeli and Palestinian flags; police returned it after cutting out the Palestinian flag, calling the display illegal.

Reuters reported that Israel expanded the restricted military zone in Gaza, placing nearly two-thirds of the territory under effective control and requiring humanitarian organizations to coordinate movements with the military, leading to reduced aid access and fear among displaced Palestinians.

Israel announced it successfully intercepted all vessels from the Gaza-bound flotilla, removed all participants unharmed, and will disembark them in Greece, reiterating the naval blockade will not be breached.

Netanyahu congratulated the Navy for preventing what he described as a Hamas-supporting flotilla from reaching Gaza, stating participants will return to their countries of origin and watch Gaza on YouTube.
Hamas's Radaa security force released video of what it claimed was an ambush on anti-Hamas militiamen near Khan Yunis, saying several were wounded.
Flotilla activist Hüseyin Oral alleges that Israeli soldiers beat him and stole his money and ID while he was detained during the raid.
Reuters reported that the U.S. is shutting its main coordination hub (CMCC) for Gaza and folding it into a new international force with fewer U.S. troops, as the ceasefire plan remains stalled.
The IDF stated it killed three operatives and wounded a fourth in southern Gaza after they crossed the Yellow Line and approached troops.
The IDF announced that its 205th Brigade wrapped up a northern Gaza operation, destroying eight tunnels and killing dozens of militants.

Hamas released footage showing fighter Karim Arja attempting to mine an IDF tank; the driver spotted it and moved away before detonation. Additional clips showed him with an explosive drone, and Hamas said he was killed during the war.
IDF said it killed a Hamas operative in northern Gaza responsible for rocket attacks on Israel throughout the war.

The Israeli Foreign Ministry said a USAID Inspector General investigation confirmed UNRWA staff were involved with Hamas and the Oct. 7 massacre, including teachers and a social worker involved in hostage-taking.
The IDF said it killed a Hamas operative in Gaza who participated in the October 7 massacre and posed an immediate threat to forces.
The IDF struck and killed two armed Hamas operatives from the air as they moved through building ruins toward Israeli forces in northern Gaza.

items.rawSummary: An arson attempt at Kenton United Synagogue and subsequent attacks on Jewish sites in London triggered a major counter-terrorism response, arrests, a raised national threat level, and diplomatic alerts, with probes expanding to examine possible foreign links.
items.analysis: An arson attempt at Kenton United Synagogue led to arrests and a counter-terrorism sweep of eight suspects over alleged Iran-linked plots. A subsequent stabbing in Golders Green wounded two Jewish men; the attacker, Essa Suleiman, was previously known to the Prevent programme and charged with attempted murder. The UK raised its terrorism threat level to severe and the U.S. Embassy warned of Islamist and extreme right-wing threats. Authorities expanded the probe into the Golders Green attack to examine possible foreign links, citing a wave of attacks on Jewish sites. A further arson at a former synagogue in east London was confirmed by Metropolitan Police as deliberately set before dawn, causing minor damage to gates and no injuries; counter-terror police are investigating. Clashes were reported outside an Ahmadiyya Muslim Community building, while British journalist Jaafar El-Ahmar contended the stabbing was not antisemitic and blamed Israel.

keyPoints.point: British police arrested a 17-year-old boy and a 19-year-old man over an attempted arson attack on the Kenton United Synagogue in northwest London.
British counter-terrorism police arrested eight individuals linked to a series of targeted attacks on Jewish sites across London, with potential links to Iran under investigation.
At least two Jewish men were stabbed in an attack in Golders Green; the suspect was arrested and one victim was left in critical condition.
Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia claimed responsibility for the London stabbing; the group has previously targeted Jewish communities across Western Europe.
Prime Minister Keir Starmer chaired an emergency COBR meeting in response to the Golders Green stabbing attack on the Jewish community.
The Golders Green attacker was identified as a 45-year-old British national born in Somalia.
British counter-terrorism police confirmed the Golders Green attacker was already known to the government's Prevent radicalisation programme.
The UK raised its terrorism threat level to 'severe', warning that further attacks are highly likely following the London attack.
The Golders Green attacker, Essa Suleiman, a British national born in Somalia, was charged with two counts of attempted murder.

Abdullah Albadri, who arrived in the UK by small boat 16 days earlier, was found guilty of preparing an attack on the Israeli Embassy in London after being caught with two knives attempting to climb into the embassy; he had previously been deported from the UK.
The U.S. Embassy in London stated that the raised UK terrorism threat level was driven by a rise in Islamist and extreme right-wing terrorist threats.
The U.S. Embassy in London warned U.S. citizens in the UK to stay alert after Britain raised its terrorism threat level to 'severe' (second-highest).
Sharren Haskel accused Zack Polanski of legitimizing violence after his response to the Golders Green stabbing drew criticism; Polanski later apologized, saying he had shared the post in haste.
Clashes were reported outside a building linked to the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community in the UK, with crowds gathering and authorities monitoring the situation.
British journalist Jaafar El-Ahmar stated that the stabbing of two London Jews was not an antisemitic attack and that Israel bears most of the responsibility.
UK counterterror police said the Golders Green stabbing was part of a wave of attacks on Jewish sites and announced an expanded probe examining possible foreign links.

Counter-terror police are investigating an arson attack at a former synagogue in east London; Metropolitan Police reported the fire was deliberately set, causing minor damage to gates and no injuries.

items.rawSummary: The U.S. naval blockade off Iran persists with active escort operations and carrier deployments, while an Iranian cruise missile wounded crew on a French cargo ship and unconfirmed reports indicate further Iranian attacks on U.S. warships in recent days.
items.analysis: U.S. naval forces continue to enforce a blockade off Iran, conducting escort missions for commercial vessels and deploying the USS George H.W. Bush to the Persian Gulf. On May 5, President Trump stated that 'Project Freedom'—an operation in the Strait of Hormuz—was paused at Pakistan's request, even as negotiations with Iran progressed; the blockade itself remains unchanged. That same day, a reported Iranian cruise missile struck the French‑owned cargo ship CGM San Antonio in the Gulf, injuring several Filipino crew members; U.S. officials cited by CBS said the weapon was a cruise missile, and the UK Maritime Trade Operations subsequently logged three separate incidents in the region. Trump linked the strike to a previous barrage of 111 Iranian missiles against a U.S. aircraft carrier weeks earlier, none of which hit. On May 6, unconfirmed reports emerged that Iran had launched additional missiles into the Gulf and fired on U.S. destroyers on May 4 and 5, though no immediate official comment was available. The commercial shipping environment remains highly dangerous, with U.S. escort and mine‑clearing efforts ongoing alongside the blockade.
items.locationName: Persian Gulf / international waters off Iran

keyPoints.point: U.S. Navy MQ-4C Triton drone is damaged mid-flight over the Persian Gulf; lands safely with no injuries.
President Trump says the naval blockade is 'unbelievable, powerful, 100%' and that negotiations with Iran are ongoing, though their negotiating teams are 'disjointed.'
CENTCOM reports that 45 commercial vessels have been directed to turn around or return to port under the ongoing naval blockade enforcement.

President Trump announces that the U.S. will begin escorting ships out of the Persian Gulf to evacuate them from months‑long internment caused by the Iran war, and warns that any interference will be met with force.
Super Hornet fighter jets launched from the USS Abraham Lincoln as part of blockade enforcement operations.
A U.S. Air Force KC‑46A tanker transmits an emergency distress code (7700) over the Persian Gulf, the second such emergency involving a U.S. Air Force refueling tanker during the blockade.
U.S. warships begin escorting commercial vessels out of the Persian Gulf; Maersk reportedly took the risk and successfully sailed through cleared paths free of mines.
CENTCOM announces the USS George H.W. Bush (CVN 77) has entered the Persian Gulf with more than 60 aircraft aboard to enforce the naval blockade and support Project Freedom in the Strait of Hormuz.
President Trump announces that 'Project Freedom' has been paused at Pakistan's request, while negotiations with Iran advance and the naval blockade remains in effect.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported three separate incidents in the Gulf region following the cruise missile strike on the French‑owned CGM San Antonio, according to CBS citing U.S. officials.

Unconfirmed reports state that on May 4 and 5 Iran launched multiple missiles into the Gulf and opened fire on U.S. destroyers.

items.rawSummary: Tensions near the Strait of Hormuz persist after an IRGC attack on a bulk carrier, the launch of US-led Project Freedom operations that destroyed Iranian small boats, and an unconfirmed claim by Iranian state media that the mission has been temporarily suspended.
items.analysis: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that a bulk carrier, likely the Liberian-flagged Minoan Falcon, was attacked by multiple small craft 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran on May 3, with all crew safe. Iran’s Fars News Agency claimed a vessel was detained for ignoring warnings, though it remained unclear if this was the same incident. The Institute for the Study of War assessed that the IRGC Navy likely carried out the attack to sustain high shipping costs and oil prices as leverage against the United States. In response, President Trump announced ‘Project Freedom’, a mission to guide neutral ships without naval escorts, and warned of force against interference, while Iranian officials threatened to treat any US intervention as a ceasefire violation and ordered the US Navy to stay out of the strait. A tanker north of Fujairah was struck by IRGC projectiles and ships near Ras Al Khaimah received VHF orders to leave anchorage, heightening regional alarm. CENTCOM subsequently reported that US Navy MH-60 Sea Hawks and Army AH-64 Apaches destroyed Iranian small boats threatening commercial shipping under Project Freedom, marking a direct military engagement. On May 6, Iran’s state TV Fars claimed President Trump announced a temporary suspension of the military plan after Iranian warnings, though this has not been confirmed by US officials, leaving the status of the operation uncertain.

items.rawSummary: The U.S. announced a proposed UN Security Council resolution on the Strait of Hormuz as oil prices plummeted on reports of an imminent U.S.-Iran deal, while pro-Palestinian protests near UN headquarters escalated into clashes with police.
items.analysis: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced a proposed UN Security Council resolution addressing the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has severely disrupted global energy shipments. Oil prices crashed more than 12% below $90 per barrel on reports that the U.S. and Iran are on the verge of a deal to end the war, a potential breakthrough in the crisis. Protests near UN headquarters have continued, with pro-Palestinian demonstrators clashing with police and destroying barricades early on May 6 after calling for an intifada the previous evening.
